name: Pre-hit dropout (silence before the reveal)

source.description: An inspected product film (batch 1, 2026-11-26) drops its soundtrack to near silence for half a second right before the key reveal accent; the same move is earshot's mixing advice (pull the music down 6-12 dB for 0.3-0.5 s before a hit).

technique: Just before the single most important reveal, take the music (and effects) out for 0.3-0.6 s, hold the picture in near-stillness, then land the reveal and its hit on the returning sound. Contrast, not loudness, makes it the biggest moment.
purpose: Make one reveal per film land hardest; create anticipation without a riser.
visual_behaviour: The picture slows or holds on the approach (an object about to meet its target); on the hit frame the element lands and motion resumes.
mechanics: Mix: bed gain -inf (or -12 dB) from hit - 0.5 s to hit, restore on the hit with a 10-30 ms fade; the hit's onset on the reveal frame. Picture: the approach eases in (slow) during the gap; no new elements enter in the gap.

decomposition.timing: Gap 0.3-0.6 s; once (at most twice) per film.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Seconds of dropout before the hit

parameters.name: depth_db
parameters.description: How far the bed drops (-inf = silence)

use_cases: the key 'it works' moment of a demo
the answer after a question in an explainer
failure_modes: Used more than once or twice it stops being a surprise
Never drop out under a spoken word: in narrated films place it in a narration pause
A gap with moving picture and no sound feels like a fault; slow the picture too

implementation.approach: Audio side: volume automation on the bed in the mux (ffmpeg volume=enable='between(t,a,b)':volume=0) or earshot kit mix.stop_down; visual side: an ease-in approach that lands on the cue. Verify the gap with reference-corpus.py listen (silences) or earshot timeline on the render.

requirements: bed gain automation in the mix

provenance.observed: The soundtrack falls below -50 dBFS from 5.50 to 6.01 s, then an accent lands at 6.06 s as the paper receipt meets its matching transaction row.
The sound falls silent for 0.9 s (5.13-6.04 s), then the accent lands as the first word of a stacked list takes its full stop.

Full silence 12.00-12.54 s while a tiny mark holds in the dark; the product name lands with a warm bloom and the hit at 12.56 s. An earlier partial dip (about 25 dB, 6.9-7.5 s) prepares the shatter at 7.55 s.
After the name, the level falls to -39.6 dB (film median -17.2 dB) for 0.93 s (1.07-2.00 s); the body enters at 2.09-2.28 s (-10.3 dB) as the orange bloom fills the frame.
Onsets stop at 13.65 s and the level falls to -37.7 dB (film median -17.6 dB) for 0.46 s (13.89-14.35 s); the hit lands at 14.42 s with a light burst and ring on the finished mark.
Between the logo badge and the first headline the level falls to -36 dB (film median -16.1 dB) over 1.44-1.90 s and returns to -14.7 dB at 2.0 s as the headline lands.
Level dips 22.6 dB under the film median at 1.44-2.28 s before the scan band and its accent grid, and 27.9 dB at 12.68-12.96 s during the ring burst before the end card.

licensing_notes: Technique only, measured from a user-supplied reference (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
